v.rationale:
I ranked them impl-2 first, impl-1 second and impl-3 last. All three test suites pass: 12 tests in impl-2, 10 in impl-1 and 16 in impl-3. I ran throwaway probes against each one: sparse ids, an order placed later by the old app version, re-running after a customer is deleted, and an empty or array-valued status. Every probe file was deleted afterwards. No MySQL server was reachable, so I checked the MySQL behaviour by reading the code and confirmed the schema calls exist in the installed Laravel source.

impl-2 handles the large-table schema change best. It splits the release into four migrations: an INSTANT column add, two online index builds (one per query shape), and the FK added in place with nullOnDelete. Each step uses Laravel 13's own API, so a failure can be retried step by step. Its backfill is correct and resumable, the empty-status case still returns all orders and is tested, and the tests cover the important edge cases. Its only real weakness is that the backfill UPDATE is raw SQL.

impl-1 makes the same database choices, and adds a useful tie-break so pagination order is stable. However, it hand-writes the MySQL ALTER statements and the foreign-key-checks toggle inside a branch on the database driver. So the code that runs in production is never exercised by the tests, and four separate DDL statements in one migration cannot be resumed cleanly if one fails partway.

impl-3 has the most idiomatic backfill and the broadest tests, but it has two real problems. Its new FormRequest makes `?status=` return 422 instead of all orders, which breaks existing callers of a heavily used endpoint (my probe confirmed this). Its first migration also puts the column add and an index build in one ALTER, which turns an instant change into a rebuild of the 20M-row table, and it has no index for requests without a status filter.
